title: Calculus starters
blurb: Derivatives and integrals, each with its one-line move.

power.name: Power rule
power.phrase: Bring the power down in front, then take one off the power.
steps: Multiply by the power.
Lower the power by 1.
A constant on its own becomes 0.
power.exception: Products need the product rule. Brackets inside brackets need the chain rule. The derivative of 7 is 0, not 7.

product.name: Product rule
steps: Name the two factors: first u, second v.
Keep the first, times the derivative of the second: u v′.
Add the second times the derivative of the first: v u′.
Tidy up.
product.exception: The derivative of a product is not the product of the derivatives: d/dx (x · x) is 2x, not 1. If one factor is just a number, keep it in front; no product rule needed.

chain.name: Chain rule
chain.phrase: Derivative of the outside, keep the inside, times derivative of the inside.
steps: Spot the inside (the bracket) and the outside (what is done to it).
Differentiate the outside, leaving the inside alone.
Multiply by the derivative of the inside.
chain.exception: Don’t forget the last “times”: d/dx (3x + 1)⁵ is 15(3x + 1)⁴, not 5(3x + 1)⁴. Keep the inside unchanged inside the outside’s derivative.

trigdiff.name: Derivatives of sin and cos
trigdiff.phrase: sin → cos → −sin → −cos → sin: each derivative is one step round the cycle.
trigdiff.also: Four steps bring you back to the start.
steps: Write the cycle: sin x, cos x, −sin x, −cos x.
Each derivative moves one step to the right.
After −cos x, go back to sin x.
Numbers in front just come along.
trigdiff.exception: Only in radians. In degrees, an extra π/180 appears. Watch the sign: d/dx cos x is −sin x, not sin x.

quotient.name: Quotient rule
quotient.phrase: Low d-high minus high d-low, over the low squared.
steps: Low = bottom, high = top, d = derivative of.
Low × d(high) minus high × d(low).
Divide by the bottom squared.
quotient.exception: Order matters because of the minus: high d-low first gives the wrong sign. If the bottom is a constant, just divide; no quotient rule needed.

integral.name: Integrating powers
integral.phrase: Raise the power by one, divide by the new power, and add C.
steps: Add 1 to the power.
Divide by that new power.
Add + C for the missing constant.
integral.exception: The rule breaks at x⁻¹, because you would divide by 0. ∫ 1/x dx = ln|x| + C.

logdef.name: What a log means
logdef.also: log₂ 8 = 3 means 2³ = 8. The base stays the base.
steps: Read log₂ 8 as “2 to what power gives 8?”
Write it as a power: 2^? = 8.
2³ = 8, so log₂ 8 = 3.
log with no base means base 10.
logdef.exception: You can only take the log of a positive number: log₂ 0 and log₂(−4) do not exist. For every base, log 1 = 0 and the log of the base itself is 1.

loglaws.name: Log laws
loglaws.phrase: Multiply → add, divide → subtract, power → front.
steps: log(mn) = log m + log n.
log(m ÷ n) = log m − log n.
log(mᵏ) = k log m.
Use them backwards to squash several logs into one.
loglaws.exception: There is no rule for log(m + n): it is not log m + log n. log m ÷ log n is not log(m ÷ n). Every log must have the same base.

liate-parts.name: Integration by parts (LIATE)
liate-parts.phrase: LIATE: prefer u from Logarithmic, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential (earlier wins).
steps: Choose u via LIATE (flexibly).
dv is the rest of the integrand.
Apply ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du.
liate-parts.exception: Heuristic, not a theorem — some integrals need the opposite choice or cyclic methods.

u-sub-chain-reverse.name: u-substitution
u-sub-chain-reverse.phrase: If you see f(g(x))·g'(x), let u = g(x) (undo the chain rule).
steps: Set u = the inner function.
Write du = u' dx.
Rewrite the integral in u.
Integrate.
Back-substitute, or convert limits for definite integrals.
u-sub-chain-reverse.exception: Watch constant factors. For definite integrals, change limits to u-values (or substitute back).

wordkeys11.name: Rate-word clues
wordkeys11.phrase: Rate, slope, marginal, instantaneous — those words point to a derivative.
steps: Spot rate-of-change language.
Differentiate the model.
Plug in the instant asked.
wordkeys11.exception: Average rate is Δy/Δx — not the derivative unless the window shrinks to an instant.

estimate11.name: Linear estimate
estimate11.phrase: Near a point: Δy ≈ y′ · Δx — the tangent’s rise.
steps: Find y′ at the known point.
Multiply by the small Δx.
Add to the known y.
estimate11.exception: Far from the point, the tangent estimate drifts — use a better model.

powerarith.name: Power rule arithmetic
powerarith.phrase: Bring the power down, then subtract one from the power.
steps: For axⁿ, derivative is a·n·xⁿ⁻¹.
Multiply the coefficient by the old power.
Reduce the power by 1.
powerarith.exception: Derivative of a constant is 0, not the constant.

commute11.name: Sum rule
commute11.phrase: Derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives — term by term.
steps: Split the expression into terms.
Differentiate each term.
Add the results.
commute11.exception: Products need the product rule — don’t term-by-term a product.

distrib11.name: Constant multiple rule
distrib11.phrase: Constants factor out of derivatives: (c·f)′ = c·f′.
steps: Pull the constant out.
Differentiate the leftover function.
Multiply back by the constant.
distrib11.exception: The constant must not depend on x.

intarith.name: Integral power arithmetic
intarith.phrase: Raise the power by one, then divide by the new power — plus C.
steps: Add 1 to the exponent.
Divide by that new exponent.
Add + C for indefinite integrals.
intarith.exception: ∫x⁻¹ dx is ln|x| + C, not x⁰/0.

mental11.name: Mental derivatives
mental11.phrase: sin → cos → −sin → −cos → sin: walk one step around the cycle.
steps: Know the four-step cycle for sin/cos.
A minus appears when you leave cos toward −sin.
Chain rule multiplies an extra inside derivative.
mental11.exception: d/dx[cos x] = −sin x — don’t drop the minus.

logarith.name: Log arithmetics
logarith.phrase: log asks: what power? Multiply → add, divide → subtract, power → front.
steps: Rewrite the log question as an exponential.
Apply log laws to expand or condense.
Solve for the unknown.
logarith.exception: log(a + b) is not log a + log b.

ftc-inverses.name: Fundamental theorem
ftc-inverses.phrase: Differentiation and integration undo each other (Fundamental Theorem).
steps: Recognize an antiderivative F of f.
For a definite integral, compute F(b) − F(a).
Read the result as net change when f is a rate.
ftc-inverses.exception: Needs continuity hypotheses. +C for indefinite integrals. √(x²)=|x|. Limits matter for definite integrals.

pvalue-row-boat.name: What a p-value is
pvalue-row-boat.phrase: A p-value is the chance, assuming H₀ is true, of data at least this extreme.
steps: State H₀ clearly.
Compute the test statistic from the data.
Find the tail probability under H₀.
Interpret cautiously — small p means surprising under H₀, not “H₀ is false with probability p”.
pvalue-row-boat.exception: p is not P(H₀ true). Small p suggests incompatibility with H₀ under the model — not proof. Avoid p-hacking.

boxplot-iqr-leash.name: Boxplot whiskers (1.5 IQR)
boxplot-iqr-leash.phrase: Boxplot whiskers reach the furthest point within 1.5 × IQR of the quartiles; beyond that are outliers.
steps: Find Q1, Q3, and IQR = Q3 − Q1.
Fences sit at Q1 − 1.5·IQR and Q3 + 1.5·IQR.
Whiskers stretch to the furthest data points still inside the fences; points beyond are outliers.
boxplot-iqr-leash.exception: Some software/curricula use different fences (or min/max whiskers). Check the convention.
